findings.title: Call to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments won't compile
findings.body: The only declaration is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at UsernamePasswordForm.java:160. Nothing in services declares a no-argument overload, and a grep for `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(` finds only these four places. So `services` fails to compile. Even if you just pass `context.getUser()`, the check is still wrong, because of the inverted condition reported in the next finding.

findings.title: Passkey conditional UI is now only set up when a user is already set, so a normal first login loses passkeys
findings.body:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns `... && user != null`. Before this change, `fillContextForm` ran exactly when the user was *not* yet identified: in the `else` branch of `authenticate`, and in `challenge` behind `context.getUser() == null`.

Now, on a fresh login (`context.getUser()` is null at line 115), `fillContextForm` is never called. The login page then has no WebAuthn challenge or `webauth` form, and passkey login is impossible. The new tests themselves expect `//form[@id='webauth']` on the first login page (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:196, :238), so they would fail.

The same applies to the error path at line 137: when the username is unknown, the user stays null and the passkey data is dropped. The PR's goal of also enabling passkeys during re-authentication needs the check to be just `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`, without the user condition. Re-authentication with a passkey is still safe without it: `WebAuthnAuthenticator.action` rejects a different user (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:201-209), and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` returns false, so no credential list is leaked.

findings.title: Missing `@Override` on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`
findings.body: This method overrides `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:128), but it has no `@Override`. If the base method is ever renamed, this override would silently stop applying, and the form would start listing the user's credentials during conditional login.

findings.title: Test name says the user has no passkey, but the test disables passkeys for the whole realm
findings.body:
`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`. That means it never covers the case its name and the comment at line 304 describe: passkeys enabled for the realm, re-authenticating a user who has no passkey. Under the intended behaviour, that user would still see the conditional passkey UI. Either rename the test or add the realm-enabled case.

Separately, the `try { findElement(...); fail(...) } catch (Exception)` pattern at lines 291-296 and 312-317 only works because `AssertionError` is not an `Exception`. `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`, as used in the organization test, would be clearer.

contracts.action: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate/challenge now call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)
contracts.equivalent_path: Before the change, fillContextForm ran when the user was null (the else branch, and challenge's `getUser()==null` guard)
contracts.before_after: Before: passkey data was filled for anonymous login only. After: it is filled only when a user is already set, so the anonymous case is lost.
contracts.visible_effect: Passkey/webauth form missing on a normal first login page
contracts.failure_mode: Users can't log in with a passkey from the regular login page; nothing shows them an error

contracts.action: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator suppresses ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS even when the user is set; passkey action during re-authentication
contracts.equivalent_path: WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm uses the user's credentials in the 2FA case
contracts.before_after: IS_USER_IDENTIFIED=false and no credential list; action still checks that the passkey's user handle matches the user already set
contracts.visible_effect: The passkey prompt is discoverable-only during re-authentication
contracts.failure_mode: A passkey for a different user is rejected with WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER

summary: Two blockers. First, UsernameForm.java:47 calls a no-argument `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` that doesn't exist, so `services` won't compile. Second, the new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` requires `user != null`. That reverses the old behaviour: passkey conditional UI is now set up only during re-authentication and is dropped from the normal first login page, which the PR's own tests expect to show it. Re-authenticating with a passkey stays safe, because the action already rejects a passkey for a different user. Also two minor points: a missing `@Override`, and a test whose name doesn't match what it covers.
